title: Book 4 — Melpomene, Chapter 95
paragraphs: This Salmoxis, I hear from the Hellenes who dwell about the Hellespont and the Pontus, was a man, and became a slave in Samos—a slave, in fact, of Pythagoras son of Mnesarchos. After becoming free, he gained great wealth and afterwards returned to his own land. Since the Thracians live hardly and are rather simple-minded, this Salmoxis, being acquainted with the Ionian way of life and with manners more cultivated than the Thracians were used to see—for he had associated with Hellenes, and not least with Pythagoras, who was no mean philosopher among them—prepared a banqueting hall, where he received and feasted the chief men of the tribe, instructing them meanwhile that neither he himself nor his guests nor their descendants in succession after them would die; but that they would come to a place where they would live forever and have all things good. While doing and saying these things, he was meanwhile making for himself a chamber under the ground. When his chamber was finished, he disappeared from among the Thracians and went down into the underground chamber, where he continued to live for three years. They grieved for his loss and mourned for him as dead. Then in the fourth year he appeared to the Thracians, and in this way what Salmoxis said became credible to them.
